hook: Walk down Bolsa Avenue in Westminster, California, and the signs switch to Vietnamese: noodle houses, markets, a Buddhist temple with a curved tile roof. Nothing about the land itself is Vietnamese. People put those marks there. Reading a street like a page of history is what this topic teaches.

prereq.q: Which of these is a culture trait?
options: The style of a group's houses
The height of a nearby hill
prereq.why: A culture trait is something people learn and share, such as a building style. Hills, rain and rocks are physical.

prereq.q: Many families from one town in Mexico settle in the same neighborhood of Chicago because relatives already live there. What kind of migration is this?
prereq.why: Chain migration is moving to a place because family or friends from home already live there.

figure.caption: Sequent occupance: each period leaves marks that the next period reuses or builds on (an invented place).

chain.cause: A group settles in a place and uses the land
chain.effect: it adds buildings, farms, signs and places of worship: its cultural landscape

chain.cause: Later groups arrive or the economy changes
chain.effect: they reuse, change or replace those marks, so the landscape builds up in layers (sequent occupance)

chain.cause: Migrants of one ethnicity settle near relatives and shared services
chain.effect: an ethnic neighborhood forms, with signs, shops and temples that serve the group

chain.cause: Ideas about gender and ethnicity change in a society
chain.effect: who uses which spaces changes, and the built landscape follows

ideas: The cultural landscape is the land as people have changed it: fields, buildings, signs, roads and places of worship laid over the physical landscape.
Sequent occupance is the idea that each group that occupies a place leaves marks that later groups keep, change or reuse, so a landscape has layers, as at St. Anthony Falls in Minneapolis.

Traditional architecture follows a long-standing local style and local materials (an adobe home, a Navajo hogan). Postmodern architecture, from about the 1970s on, mixes styles on purpose and looks similar in many cities.
Ethnicity is identity with a group that shares ancestry and traditions. An ethnic neighborhood is an area where one ethnic group is concentrated, visible in its signs, shops and places of worship.

misconception.wrong: The cultural landscape is the natural scenery of a place: its mountains, rivers and forests.
misconception.right: Those are the physical landscape. The cultural landscape is what people have added or changed: in the Douro Valley of Portugal, the river is physical, but the vineyards planted on the slopes are cultural.

summary: The cultural landscape is the human imprint on the land: buildings, fields, signs and places of worship. Landscapes build up in layers as each group leaves marks the next one reuses, which is sequent occupance. Architecture can be traditional (local styles and materials) or postmodern (mixed styles from about the 1970s on). Ethnicity, gender and Indigenous ways of life all shape space, from ethnic neighborhoods such as Little Saigon to the hogans of the Navajo Nation.
